calls.reason: ARC Prize documents substantial generalization gains, while the AGI Society finds AGI unestablished. Neither establishes whether alternative approaches are necessary.

Lake and Baroni tentatively link generalization weaknesses to data demand; NYT reporting links data demand to licensing choices. The evidence does not clearly connect those choices to generalization weaknesses.

The statement expresses an expectation. The cited studies show diminishing returns in small-model or repeated-data settings, while sparse training delays saturation; the broader claim remains unclear.

Epoch projects a public-text shortage rather than documenting one. Synthetic-data experiments show conditional benefits, and Musk's exhaustion assertion lacks measurements establishing the broader shortage.
OMEGA documents persistent generalization failures, while the length-generalization and fluid-reasoning studies show improvements. These bounded results cannot settle permanent data insufficiency.

The NeurIPS studies show planning collapsing after name changes and reasoning failing beyond training distributions. Targeted meta-learning successes qualify, but do not overturn, the claimed limitation in common configurations.
